title: UBC Quarto brand
text:
ubc-quarto-brand
A Quarto extension that gives a UBC course book the brand the DSCI 521 book was built with: the UBC colour palette, Atkinson Hyperlegible fonts, light and dark modes, callouts with icons, labelled code listings, a console window, and themed quizzes.
See it: the demo book at https://ubc-mds.github.io/ubc-quarto-brand/ renders every part of the brand.

title: 2  Conventions in the Book
text:
2.1 Text
One page holding every construct the book uses, so a theme or CSS change can be checked in one place, in both light and dark mode. This is a good reference page for how source code renders to the page.
You can learn more about features in the Quarto Guide.
Body text, with bold, italic, inline code, a link to another page and an external link. Keyboard keys are written with <kbd>. Named keys take title case: Ctrl, Shift, Tab, Enter, Esc, Space, Up, Down. A letter key stays lowercase unless Shift is genuinely part of the shortcut, so that an uppercase letter never implies a Shift that isn’t there: Ctrl + c interrupts a command, while Ctrl + Shift + C opens the browser console. The same rule reads correctly for a program that treats case as meaning, such as n and N in less. Enough of them to wrap, so their boxes can be checked against each other on neighbouring lines: press Ctrl + c to stop a running command, Ctrl + d to close the shell, Tab to complete a path, Up and Down to walk back through your history, and Ctrl + r to search it.

title: 2  Conventions in the Book
text:
2.4 Quizzes
Quizzes are written in a quizdown fence and rendered by _extensions/quizdown, a fork of quizdown-js kept at UBC-MDS/quarto-quizdown-mds-ext. The fence never says which kind of question it holds – the type comes out of the shape of the list you write:







You write
You get




an unordered list whose items hold ::
matching: drag a chip into a slot


an ordered list with no checkboxes
sequence: drag the lines into order


an unordered list of - [ ] and - [x]
multiple choice: tick every right answer


an ordered list of 1. [ ] and 1. [x]
single choice: tick the one right answer



Three optional pieces work in all four: a --- block of options above the question, a > blockquote under the heading, which becomes a hint behind a button, and a > blockquote indented under one answer, which becomes the feedback shown for that answer once the quiz is marked.
A quiz renders into a shadow root, which is a corner of the page that no stylesheet can reach into from outside. So the colours below do not come from styles.scss like everything else on this page – they come from quizdown-theme.html, which injects one stylesheet into each quiz. That is the thing all four of these are really here to check.
The book only uses the first two types so far. The other two are on this page anyway, because an unused construct is the one that breaks without anyone noticing.

2.4.1 Matching
Options, a hint and per-answer feedback, which the other three take the same way. An item with nothing on the left of its :: is a distractor: it joins the pool of chips but matches no prompt.

---
shuffle_answers: true
---

## Match each command to what it does

> Every one of these appears in the first lecture.

- `pwd` :: prints the directory you are in

    > Print Working Directory.

- `ls` :: lists what is beside you
- `cd` :: moves you somewhere else
- :: prints your username



2.4.2 Sequence

## Put the steps of one trip around the shell's loop in order

You type `ls -F` after the `$` prompt and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>.

1. The shell takes in the line you typed
2. The shell finds the `ls` program and runs it with the `-F` option
3. The program's output is written to the terminal
4. A fresh `$` prompt appears, waiting for the next command



2.4.3 Multiple choice

## Which of these are shells?

- [x] `bash`
- [x] `zsh`
- [ ] `ls`

    > `ls` is a program you run *from* a shell.

- [ ] JupyterLab



2.4.4 Single choice

## Which command prints the directory you are in?

1. [ ] `cd`
2. [x] `pwd`
3. [ ] `ls`
4. [ ] `whoami`

title: 6  ubc-quarto-brand: design spec
text:
6.3 Design
The parts and how they connect are drawn on the Architecture page.

6.3.1 The extension
One extension, ubc, in _extensions/ubc/ (Q&A 18). It contributes two things:

The brand, through metadata: project: brand: brand.yml. Quarto merges it into any project with the extension installed, whatever its format, so colours, fonts and dark mode apply even to a plain format: html page.
A ubc-html format with the theme layers (light: [brand, styles.scss, ubc.scss], dark: [brand, styles.scss, styles-dark.scss, ubc.scss, ubc-dark.scss]), the filters (code-labels.lua, custom-callout, quizdown), include-after-body: [quizdown-theme.html, ubc-quizdown.html], and the four custom callout types.

A format cannot carry the brand on its own: its brand theme layer means the project’s brand, and 521’s styles.scss needs the $brand-* variables that only the brand defines. A prototype rendered this setup, before the extension had a layer of its own, on Quarto 1.11.6, for a book and for a website (Q&A 18).

6.3.2 What a book can change
From the prototype (Q&A 18):

Add styles with an extra theme layer, light and dark as separate lists: format: ubc-html: theme: light: [extra.scss] dark: [extra.scss]. The layer comes after the extension’s, and $brand-* names work in it. A plain list (theme: [extra.scss]) crashes Quarto.
Add or recolour callout types with its own custom-callout: keys, which deep-merge over the extension’s (Q&A 19).
Turn on the MDS logo by pointing its sidebar or navbar logo at the bundled file (Q&A 16).
Not replace the brand piecemeal: a book’s own _brand.yml is silently ignored, and a top-level brand: replaces the whole brand, so it must define every colour the styles use.



6.3.3 The test book
The repository root is a Quarto book that renders with format: ubc-html, next to _extensions/ubc/ (Q&A 22, 23):

Home: the README.
Conventions: DSCI 521’s lectures/0-conventions.qmd almost as-is (Q&A 15): text, every listing kind, executed R and Python cells (Q&A 13), callouts, quizzes, tables, math, figures and tabsets. Only its links into other 521 chapters change.
Callouts: Quarto’s five built-ins (note, tip, important, warning, caution), plain and titled, the four custom types, and two exercises in a row for the numbering (Q&A 19).
Using it in a book: installing, the format line, the logo, extra styles, extra callouts, and the limits above.
Where it comes from: every file’s DSCI 521 original, linked at 991bae89cba9, and what changed (Q&A 21).
The project: the spec, the plan, the Q&A pages, the changelog and AGENTS.md, rendered from where they live.

tests/website/ is a one-page website project: a callout, a bash listing and a quiz. make copies the extension into it, git-ignored, before rendering it in CI (Q&A 10, 22).
Executed cells run through knitr, with Python through reticulate from the uv venv, as in 521. R needs knitr, rmarkdown and reticulate (renv); Python needs matplotlib (uv).


6.3.4 CI and delivery

pr.yml, on every pull request event: make check, then pr-preview-action deploys the rendered book to gh-pages under pr-preview/pr-<N>/ and comments the link, or removes the preview when the PR closes. Runs are grouped per PR and a newer event cancels an older run, so a merge mid-build leaves no stray preview (Q&A 11, 24).
publish.yml, on a push to main: the same build, then github-pages-deploy-action deploys the book to gh-pages with clean-exclude: pr-preview and force: false, so previews and the branch’s .nojekyll survive (Q&A 24).
make check: renders the test book and the website check, failing on any Quarto warning or unresolved link; runs tests/check-render.sh over the rendered HTML (the brand’s colours, both stylesheets, the labels, the callouts’ glyphs and colours, the counters, the quiz assets); runs lychee offline, actionlint and gitleaks.
Rulings: Ubuntu runner, Quarto 1.11.6 pinned and quarto-required: ">=1.11.0", Python 3.14, every third-party action pinned by commit SHA (Q&A 24).
Releases: a PR bumps version: in _extension.yml and adds a CHANGELOG.md entry; Dan tags vX.Y.Z after merging it (Q&A 17).
Straight to main: the agent commits and pushes to main; Dan reviews the extension in the adopting book’s PR, with its preview (Q&A 29). pr.yml serves anyone who opens a PR here later.

6.5 Open items and risks

Vendored dependencies: custom-callout (0.0.1-dev.3) and quizdown are copies; updating them is a manual PR.
Quizdown loads on every page, quiz or not, as in DSCI 521 (Q&A 12).
A partial brand override isn’t possible (see What a book can change); the how-to page says so.
Fork PRs get no preview: their token can’t write to the repository.
[Dan] settings: Pages from the gh-pages branch (after the first publish creates it), read and write workflow permissions, a ruleset on main.
plan-driven-development’s hooks and leak check aren’t built yet: every push of build follows make leaks.

7.1 Setup
Every question asked at kickoff, with Dan’s answer and his reason in his words.

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
Small or large? Small: one spec, one plan, no phases. Dan: “small, we can just use it in this book now. will update 521 later (already created issue to track https://github.com/UBC-MDS/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/issues/35)”.
Public or private? Public. Settled by the repository Dan created (UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand, public).
A live demo site? Yes: the test book deploys to GitHub Pages from main, and the project docs (README, spec, plan, changelog) join it as pages, so they render under the brand too (“a demo that is itself a Quarto site”). Dan chose option A, “Live test book + docs”.
Where does the repo live? GitHub, UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand, cloned to ~/git/mds/ubc-quarto-brand. Settled by the repository Dan created.
Mode? Fully vibed: the agent rules on questions that would change the spec or a decision, logs each as “decided without Dan”, and merges once CI is green. The stops that never relax still wait for Dan. Dan chose option B, “Fully vibed”.

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
7.2 Design decisions made before kickoff
These were settled while planning the same branding for the reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows book, before Dan asked for it to become this extension: “instead of moving all those brand elements into this repo as copy+paste, can we clone https://github.com/UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand into ~/git/mds/ and then move all those brand elements into a quarto extension that gets used by this book? i also like how we crfeated a convensions document in 521. we can create and use that as a test book/site in the extension too to quickly fix things”.

Callout numbering. Activity and exercise callouts are numbered automatically, per page, as in DSCI 521. In the consuming book, hand-written numbers come out of the titles. Dan chose “Auto-number, strip titles”.
Descriptive callout titles. A descriptive title (for example “Get to know Quarto”) becomes a bold first line in the callout’s body, so every title reads “Exercise N”. Dan chose “Bold first line (Recommended)”.
Callout icons and colours. Font Awesome icons and UBC palette colours for all four callout types: activity fa-person-chalkboard in ubc-blue-deep, exercise fa-dumbbell in mds-green, definition fa-book-open in ubc-gold-dark, relevance-project fa-diagram-project in ubc-blue-mid. Dan chose “FA icons + brand colours (Recommended)”.
Listing labels. DSCI 521’s code-labels.lua comes along: every bash listing is labelled “Terminal” and every out listing “Output”. Dan chose “Port it (Recommended)”.

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
7.3 Grilling

Test site shape. The deployed demo is a Quarto book: DSCI 521’s conventions page, a gallery of every callout and listing, and the project docs as chapters. A one-page website project also renders in CI only, to catch website-specific breakage before DSCI 521 adopts the extension. Dan chose “A. Book demo + website check (Recommended)”.
Commits, PRs, merging, previews. Dan, during grilling: “you may create commits and PRs, but don’t merge, the GHA for pr-preview should be able to render the site for me to also review”. So the agent commits, pushes the work branch and opens PRs, but never merges: every merge waits for Dan, overriding fully vibed’s merge. Every PR gets a rendered preview of the test book through pr-preview-action, as in the reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows book, so the demo deploys from a gh-pages branch (pr-preview-action needs “Deploy from branch”), not from actions/deploy-pages as plan-driven-development’s docs-site default gives. Asked whether this was meant only for the book’s PR #37, Dan confirmed it applies here: “the dont’ merge and we’ll wait for PR previews for final check is for this current set of quarot ubc branding”.
DSCI 521’s extra pieces. The extension carries both: the quizdown quizzes (the quizdown extension embedded, its shadow-root theme include, and the quiz colour variables) and the .term console window, so DSCI 521 adopts the extension by deleting its local copies. Every consumer carries quizdown’s JavaScript, used or not. Dan chose “A. Both in the extension” over the recommended “B. Console in, quizzes stay”.
Executed cells in the test book. The test book keeps the executed {r} and {python} cells, so executed output is tested under the brand in every PR preview. CI installs a minimal environment: R with knitr, rmarkdown and reticulate through renv, and Python through uv. Dan chose “A. Run R + Python (Recommended)”.
Fonts. Atkinson Hyperlegible Next and Mono load from Google Fonts (source: google), as in DSCI 521, so every reader’s browser requests them from Google. Dan chose “B. Google Fonts” over the recommended “A. Bundled files”, which would have shipped the OFL-licensed woff2 files in the extension so that no third party is contacted. Dan: “good fonts are not privacy concern”.
The conventions page. The test book’s conventions page mimics DSCI 521’s lectures/0-conventions.qmd almost as-is, Quizzes section and executed cells included. Dan: “we should try to mimic that convensions file almost as-is it shows almost eveything that we use in a book.”
Identity and logo. The extension ships no book name or links: each book keeps its title and links in its own _quarto.yml. It bundles DSCI 521’s MDSlogo.png as an available asset, not applied by default; an MDS book turns it on with one line in its _quarto.yml. The UBC logo is not bundled. Dan chose “C. MDS logo, opt-in” over the recommended “A. Brand only, books add theirs”.
Versioning. _extension.yml carries a semantic version, and Dan tags releases (v0.1.0, and on). A book installs a tag, quarto add UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.1.0, and updates in its own PR with quarto update, where the PR preview shows the change. CHANGELOG.md lists each release. Tags are a stop that never relaxes, so each release is a step for Dan. Dan chose “A. Tagged releases (Recommended)”.
Packaging. One extension, ubc, contributing the brand through metadata: project: brand: brand.yml and a ubc-html format (the light and dark theme layers, code-labels.lua, and the embedded custom-callout and quizdown extensions). A book runs quarto add UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.1.0 and sets format: ubc-html; it adds its own styles as an extra theme layer (format: ubc-html: theme: light: [extra.scss] dark: [extra.scss]). A prototype rendered this exact setup on Quarto 1.11.6 for a book and a website. Dan chose “A. One ubc extension (Recommended)”.
Callouts. Dan: “we should have all callout examples, built-ins and new ones”. Read as: the extension defines all four custom callout types (activity, exercise, definition, relevance-project), and the test book’s gallery shows every callout, Quarto’s five built-ins (note, tip, important, warning, caution) and the four custom ones, so each is checked under the brand. A book can still recolour a type or add its own in its _quarto.yml: the prototype showed a book’s custom-callout: settings deep-merge over the extension’s.
Shared understanding. Dan confirmed the grilling summary and moved kickoff on to the design: “Yes, go to the design (Recommended)”.
Provenance in the docs. Dan: “when we document this new quarto extension we should document how it comes from 521”. The docs explain, file by file, which DSCI 521 file each piece of the extension comes from and what changed on the way, linking to 521’s originals.

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
7.4 Design sections

Section 1, layout and contents. The test book lives at the repository root next to _extensions/ubc/ (Quarto finds extensions only in a project’s own _extensions/). The extension holds DSCI 521’s files as of commit 991bae89cba9, unchanged apart from brand.yml losing 521’s name and links and the format gaining the definition and relevance-project callouts. The website check renders a git-ignored copy of the extension. Dan chose “A. Approve section 1 (Recommended)”.
Section 2, the test book. Pages: Home (the README), Conventions (DSCI 521’s page almost as-is), Callouts (the five built-ins, titled and plain, the four custom types, and two exercises in a row for numbering), Using it in a book (the how-to), Where it comes from (provenance, pinned to 521 at 991bae89cba9), and the project docs as chapters rendered from where they live. tests/website/ is one page rendered as a website in CI. Dan chose “A. Approve section 2 (Recommended)”.
Section 3, CI, delivery and adoption. pr.yml runs make check and deploys a preview with pr-preview-action, cancelling a PR’s in-flight run when a newer event arrives; publish.yml deploys main to gh-pages with github-pages-deploy-action (clean-exclude: pr-preview, force: false). make check renders the test book and the website check, runs lychee offline, actionlint and gitleaks. Rulings: Ubuntu runner, Quarto 1.11.6 pinned with quarto-required: ">=1.11.0", Python 3.14, third-party actions pinned by SHA. Releases: a PR bumps the version and CHANGELOG, Dan tags after merging. The reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows book adopts v0.1.0 in its own PR afterwards. Dan chose “A. Approve section 3 (Recommended)”.

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
7.5 After the plan

Other Quarto outputs, a stretch goal. Dan: “if possible we should see if this will work for the quarto book/revealjs/site/document outputs. but that would be a stretch goal after this is all built”. Books and websites are already in the plan (S01, S15); a single document and revealjs slides go to the spec’s Later table as optional (S19, S20).

title: 7  ubc-quarto-brand: kickoff Q&A
text:
7.6 Review before approval
The builder check (a fresh reviewer reading the spec as its builder) raised three questions; each claim was checked against the code before Dan saw it.

Callout styling. custom-callout colours a callout’s border and fill but never its icon, and DSCI 521’s styles.scss colours only the activity and exercise icons. Quarto maps the built-ins to $blue, $green, $red, $yellow and $orange, and the brand defines no orange and nothing per mode. The extension completes the styling in its own layer after DSCI 521’s files, which stay byte-identical: coloured, spaced icons with dark-mode variants for all four custom types, and the five built-ins in brand colours per mode, caution in a derived orange that clears AA (UBC publishes no orange). DSCI 521’s built-in callouts change colour when it adopts the extension. Dan chose “A. Complete it, separate layer (Recommended)”.
Licence. A split licence, as in the reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows book: MIT for the code (Lua, SCSS, scripts, workflows) and CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 for the docs and the test book’s text. Vendored code keeps its own terms: quizdown’s MIT licence text goes beside its copy, and Font Awesome’s terms stay in its CSS. The MDS logo is excluded as UBC’s mark. custom-callout has no licence upstream (coatless-quarto/custom-callout), a redistribution gap DSCI 521 already has: [Dan] asks its author, James Balamuta, to add one. Dan chose “A. Split, like the book (Recommended)”.
Pages, approval and execution. Asked when to switch Pages on, Dan answered: “no you do everything essentially make this a working and complete one-shot. create the github action for publication too. if you need me to check off boxes i will do that now”. Read as: the spec and plan are approved, and the agent builds the whole project in one go, publish workflow included, choosing the execution method itself (inline, superpowers:executing-plans: the tasks are sequential and need this machine’s R, Python and Quarto). The agent creates an empty gh-pages branch now so that Dan can switch Pages on before the PR opens, and the PR’s own preview proves S13. Merging still waits for Dan (item 11).
Work on main; review happens in the book. Dan: “for the UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand repo, you can just do everythign on main. there is no PR review there. the pr review is just testing and using the extension in this current repo for the book”. So the agent commits and pushes to main here, with no PRs, and publish.yml deploys the demo on every push. Item 11’s “no merging, PR previews” now applies to the reproducible-and-trustworthy-workflows book’s adoption PR, where Dan reviews the extension in use. pr.yml stays, for anyone who opens a PR here later. The build branch stays as it is (deleting branches is a stop).

title: 8  ubc-quarto-brand Implementation Plan
text:
8.1 Global Constraints
Goal: A Quarto extension, ubc, that packages the DSCI 521 book’s UBC brand as a ubc-html format, with a test book at the repository root that renders every part of it and deploys as the demo.
Architecture: _extensions/ubc/ contributes the brand through metadata: project: brand: and a ubc-html format (theme layers, the code-labels filter, embedded custom-callout and quizdown). Its files are fetched from DSCI 521 at one pinned commit by scripts/fetch-521.sh. The repository root is a Quarto book using that format; tests/website/ is a one-page website using it from a GitHub-style install folder. tests/check-render.sh asserts on the rendered HTML and CSS.
Tech Stack: Quarto 1.11.6, brand.yml, SCSS, Lua filters, custom-callout 0.0.1-dev.3, quizdown 1.3.2; R 4.6.2 with renv (knitr, rmarkdown, reticulate, here); Python 3.14 with uv (matplotlib); GitHub Actions with pr-preview-action, github-pages-deploy-action and lychee-action; gitleaks 8.30.1; actionlint.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ubc-quarto-brand-design.md
Now: Task 5: The website check and the how-to, open.

title: 8  ubc-quarto-brand Implementation Plan
text:
8.2 Review Focus

A book installed from GitHub has the extension at _extensions/UBC-MDS/ubc/, not _extensions/ubc/; brand, filters and the logo path must resolve there. Task 5’s website check installs into that folder.
A page with no callout, listing or quiz must still get the fonts, colours and dark mode. Task 2 asserts on the Home page.
Dark mode’s derived colours: tab titles fall back to black on navy unless $body-emphasis-color is set. Task 2 asserts --bs-emphasis-color in the dark bundle.
A book’s own theme layer must come after the extension’s and see $brand-* names. Task 5’s website check adds one.
A pull request from a fork cannot write a preview. It is documented in the spec’s risks; no test can run it.



8.2.1 Task 1: Environment, test book skeleton and CI
Tier: 3 · Scenarios: S13, S14
Ruling: test-utc re-runs the output checks, not the render: nothing rendered depends on the time zone; costs a render-time date bug going unseen.
Ruling: the plan’s index.qmd listing escapes its shortcode ({{< … >}}), because Quarto expanded it when rendering this plan as a page; costs a reader copying three braces.
Files: - Create: .python-version, pyproject.toml, uv.lock, DESCRIPTION, renv.lock, .Rprofile, renv/activate.R, renv/settings.json, renv/.gitignore, .gitignore, _quarto.yml, index.qmd, tests/check-render.sh, .github/workflows/pr.yml, .github/workflows/publish.yml - Modify: Makefile
Interfaces: - Consumes: nothing. - Produces: make setup, make test (renders the book into _book/, fails on any Quarto WARN or ERROR, then runs tests/check-render.sh), make test-utc, make lint, make docs, make leaks, make check; tests/check-render.sh with expect <description> <pattern> <file> (case-insensitive extended regex) and exists <description> <path>, and BOOK=_book. Later tasks append sections to it.

Step 0: Record the base: git rev-parse HEAD > .git/TASK_BASE.
Step 1: Write the failing test, tests/check-render.sh, and chmod 755 it:


Terminal
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Checks the rendered test book, and from Task 5 the website check, for every
# part of the brand. Run by `make test` after the renders.
set -euo pipefail
fail=0

expect() { # expect <description> <pattern> <file>: case-insensitive extended regex
  if grep -q -i -E -- "$2" "$3" 2>/dev/null; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1 ($3)"; fail=1; fi
}
exists() { # exists <description> <path>
  if [ -e "$2" ]; then echo "ok   $1"; else echo "FAIL $1 ($2 missing)"; fail=1; fi
}

BOOK=_book

# --- Task 1: the book and the project docs render (S13, S14)
exists "home page"         "$BOOK/index.html"
exists "spec page"         "$BOOK/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ubc-quarto-brand-design.html"
exists "kickoff Q&A page"  "$BOOK/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ubc-quarto-brand-qa.html"
exists "plan page"         "$BOOK/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-30-ubc-quarto-brand.html"
exists "changelog page"    "$BOOK/CHANGELOG.html"
exists "how we work page"  "$BOOK/AGENTS.html"

exit $fail

Step 6: Replace the Makefile (GNU make 3.81):

# ubc-quarto-brand: a command anyone runs more than once is a target here (`make help`).
.PHONY: help setup hooks check test test-utc lint docs leaks clean

help: ## List the targets
    @grep -E '^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]+:.*## ' $(MAKEFILE_LIST) | awk 'BEGIN {FS = ":.*## "}; {printf "  %-10s %s\n", $$1, $$2}'

setup: ## Install the Python (uv) and R (renv) packages for the executed cells
    uv sync
    Rscript -e 'renv::restore(prompt = FALSE)'

hooks: ## Install the git hooks (none exist yet)
    @echo "No git hooks are installed yet: plan-driven-development's hooks are not built."

check: test test-utc lint docs leaks ## Everything CI runs

test: ## Render the test book, fail on any Quarto warning, then check the output
    @rm -rf _book
    uv run quarto render 2>&1 | tee .render.log
    @if grep -E 'WARN|ERROR' .render.log; then echo "Quarto warned or failed: see .render.log"; exit 1; fi
    tests/check-render.sh

test-utc: ## Re-run the output checks under TZ=UTC
    TZ=UTC tests/check-render.sh

lint: ## Lint the GitHub Actions workflows
    uvx --from actionlint-py actionlint .github/workflows/*.yml

docs: ## Check the rendered book's links (CI runs lychee if it isn't installed here)
    @if command -v lychee >/dev/null; then lychee --offline --no-progress _book; else echo "lychee not installed: the link check runs in CI"; fi

leaks: ## Scan the whole git history for secrets
    gitleaks git --redact --no-banner .

clean: ## Remove rendered output
    rm -rf _book .quarto .render.log .render-website.log tests/website/_extensions tests/website/_site tests/website/.quarto
test-utc re-runs the checks rather than the render: nothing the render produces depends on the time zone (Ruling).

Step 7: Write .github/workflows/pr.yml:

on:
  pull_request:
    branches: main
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize, closed]

name: PR preview

# One run per PR: a newer event (a push, or the PR closing) cancels an older
# run, so a merge mid-build never deploys a preview after its removal.
concurrency:
  group: preview-${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  preview:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the preview to gh-pages
      pull-requests: write # comment the preview link on the PR
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # make leaks scans the whole history

      # The build steps are skipped when the PR closes;
      # the last step then removes the preview.
      - name: Set up Quarto
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        with:
          version: 1.11.6

      - name: Set up uv
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        # third-party: pin the SHA
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:
          enable-cache: true # installs the Python in .python-version

      - name: Install Python packages
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        run: uv sync --locked

      - name: Install R
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-r@v2
        with:
          r-version: '4.6.2'

      - name: Install R packages
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        uses: r-lib/actions/setup-renv@v2

      - name: Install gitleaks
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        run: |
          cd "$RUNNER_TEMP"
          curl -sSfLO https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v8.30.1/gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz
          curl -sSfLO https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks/releases/download/v8.30.1/gitleaks_8.30.1_checksums.txt
          grep ' gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz$' gitleaks_8.30.1_checksums.txt | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf gitleaks_8.30.1_linux_x64.tar.gz gitleaks
          echo "$RUNNER_TEMP" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      - name: Render and check
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        run: make check

      - name: Check links
        if: github.event.action != 'closed'
        # third-party: pin the SHA
        uses: lycheeverse/lychee-action@e7477775783ea5526144ba13e8db5eec57747ce8 # v2.9.0
        with:
          args: --offline --no-progress _book
          fail: true

      # Deploys _book/ to gh-pages under pr-preview/pr-<N>/ and comments the
      # link, or removes the preview when the PR closes.
      - name: Deploy PR preview
        # third-party action with write access: pin the SHA
        uses: rossjrw/pr-preview-action@873417d2df72380da1f3978378fb58560bcde976 # v1.8.2
        with:
          source-dir: _book

Step 8: Write .github/workflows/publish.yml:

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    branches: main

name: Publish

jobs:
  publish:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write # push the book to gh-pages
    steps:
      - name: Check out repository
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # make leaks scans the whole history

      - name: Set up Quarto
        uses: quarto-dev/quarto-actions/setup@v2
        with:
          version: 1.11.6

      - name: Set up uv
        # third-party: pin the SHA
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@68559e99cc807c1eb7e9238fd43a15bba460eec2 # v10.3.3
        with:

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Copies the brand from the DSCI 521 book into this extension, from one pinned
# commit, so every file here can be traced to its original (the book's "Where it
# comes from" page). Usage: scripts/fetch-521.sh [commit]
set -euo pipefail
SHA="${1:-991bae89cba904ae2dd0753338c306333eb5ea2e}"
RAW="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/UBC-MDS/DSCI_521_platforms-dsci_book/$SHA"
EXT=_extensions/ubc

fetch() { # fetch <path in 521> <path here>
  mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")"
  curl -sSfL "$RAW/$1" -o "$2"
  echo "fetched $1 -> $2"
}

fetch styles.scss         "$EXT/styles.scss"
fetch styles-dark.scss    "$EXT/styles-dark.scss"
fetch code-labels.lua     "$EXT/code-labels.lua"
fetch quizdown-theme.html "$EXT/quizdown-theme.html"
fetch MDSlogo.png         "$EXT/MDSlogo.png"
for f in _extension.yml customcallout.lua fa.lua assets/css/fontawesome.css assets/webfonts/fa-solid-900.woff2; do
  fetch "_extensions/coatless-quarto/custom-callout/$f" "$EXT/_extensions/coatless-quarto/custom-callout/$f"
done
for f in _extension.yml quizdown.lua assets/quizdown-init.js assets/quizdown.js assets/quizdownHighlight.js assets/quizdownKatex.js; do

title: Callouts
---

Every callout a book can use, so a change to the brand can be checked against all
of them at once, in light and dark mode.

## Quarto's built-in callouts

::: {.callout-note}
A note, with no title.
:::

::: {.callout-note title="A titled note"}
A note with a title of its own.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
A tip, with no title.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="A titled tip"}
A tip with a title of its own.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
Something important, with no title.
:::

::: {.callout-important title="A titled important"}
Something important, with a title of its own.
:::

::: {.callout-warning}
A warning, with no title.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="A titled warning"}
A warning with a title of its own.
:::

::: {.callout-caution}
A caution, with no title.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="A titled caution"}
A caution with a title of its own.
:::

## The brand's callouts

Activities and exercises number themselves on each page, in order,
so a book writes them with no title and no number.
These two exercises read "Exercise 1" and "Exercise 2":

:::{.exercise}
The first exercise on this page.
:::

:::{.exercise}
The second exercise on this page.
:::

:::{.activity}
An activity: something the class does together.
:::

:::{.definition}
A definition of a term.
:::

:::{.relevance-project}
How this connects to the course project.
:::

A book can recolour these types or add its own:
see [Using it in a book](using.qmd).

## A console window

A captured terminal session, shown as a window so a reader recognizes it as a screen
rather than a listing to copy:

::: {.term}

---
title: Using it in a book
---

## Install it

In your Quarto book or website project, install a tagged release:

```bash
quarto add UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.1.0
```

Quarto copies the extension into `_extensions/UBC-MDS/ubc/`.
Commit that folder: your book keeps exactly this version until you update it.

## Use the format

In your `_quarto.yml`:

```yaml
format: ubc-html
```

That one line brings the theme, the listing labels, the callouts and the quizzes.
The brand's colours, fonts and dark mode apply to every page as soon as the extension
is installed, whatever format a page uses.

## Update it

```bash
quarto update UBC-MDS/ubc-quarto-brand@v0.2.0
```

Do it in a pull request of its own, so the preview shows what changed before you merge.
The [changelog](../CHANGELOG.md) lists what each release changed.

## Turn on the MDS logo

The MDS logo ships with the extension but is not shown unless you ask for it.
In a book:

```yaml
book:
  sidebar:
    logo: _extensions/UBC-MDS/ubc/MDSlogo.png
    logo-alt: "MDS logo"
```

In a website, the same two keys go under `website: sidebar:`.

## Add your own styles

Add a theme layer of your own. Give it to both modes, as two lists:

```yaml
format:
  ubc-html:
    theme:
      light: [extra.scss]
      dark: [extra.scss]
```

Your layer comes after the extension's, so its rules win,
and the brand's colours are available in it as `$brand-<name>`, for example `$brand-ubc-blue`.
A single list, `theme: [extra.scss]`, makes Quarto stop with an error.

## Add or recolour a callout type

Add `custom-callout:` keys to your `_quarto.yml`. They merge with the extension's:
a new type is added, and a type the extension already has takes your values.

```yaml
custom-callout:
  lab:
    title: "Lab"
    icon: true
    icon-symbol: "fa-flask"
    color: "#A6192E"
```

The colour must be a literal hex, because this YAML cannot read the brand's Sass.
Take it from the palette:

| Name | Hex |
|---|---|
| `ubc-blue` | `#002145` |
| `ubc-blue-deep` | `#0055B7` |
| `ubc-blue-mid` | `#0077C8` |
| `ubc-blue-bright` | `#00A7E1` |
| `ubc-gold-dark` | `#8A6D2B` |
| `mds-green` | `#1C5F2E` |
| `alert-red` | `#A6192E` |

The [Callouts](callouts.qmd) page shows every type the extension defines.

## What you cannot change

You cannot replace part of the brand.
A `_brand.yml` of your own is ignored, because the extension's brand takes its place.
A top-level `brand:` key replaces the whole brand,
so it would have to define every colour the extension's styles use, or the render fails.
To change how things look, add a theme layer instead.

## Executed code and quizzes

Executed R and Python cells need nothing from the extension.
Quizzes are written in a `quizdown` code block;
the [conventions page](book-conventions.qmd) shows each kind.

text:
10.1 Commands
Follow the plan-driven-development skill wherever the harness has it. Every session follows this file, in any harness, with or without the plan-driven-development skill: it holds every rule that runs each session, and as a user instruction it outranks every skill’s defaults (Overrides).
Size: small · Visibility: public · Demo: the test book, https://ubc-mds.github.io/ubc-quarto-brand/ (a Quarto site the docs join) · Mode: fully vibed, except merging · Check: make check · Work in place: this folder checks out main. Attended: phase PRs and the fifth stop wait for Dan; fully vibed: the agent merges and decides. Made from plan-driven-development 65072f9.
Here, the work goes straight to main: the agent commits and pushes to main, with no phase branch and no PR; publish.yml deploys the demo on every push. Dan reviews the extension in use, in the PR of the book that adopts it (Q&A 29 in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-ubc-quarto-brand-qa.md). This overrides the phase-branch, PR and merge rules below. Tags and releases still wait for Dan.
Until the hooks and the leak check exist, make hooks installs nothing and there is no denylist: every push follows a passing make leaks.
Through the Makefile (make help): make hooks, make check, make test, make test-utc, make lint, make leaks, and make docs on a site project. Name targets, never raw commands; a command anyone runs more than once becomes a target.

title: 10  ubc-quarto-brand: how we work
text:
10.2 Resume
At every session start, on “where are we?”, and after a compaction, a usage-limit stop or a restart, re-read the repo before acting, in this order; a summary drops details, the repo doesn’t.

Hooks: make hooks, before any commit. If it fails, stop and tell Dan.
This file: size, visibility, demo, mode, any worktree.
git: git fetch (if it fails, say so in one line); the active branch, the newest non-main one in git for-each-ref --sort=-committerdate refs/heads, matching the newest Plan: trailer; ahead (git log origin/<branch>..HEAD) and behind (git log HEAD..origin/<branch>), upstream set or not; worktrees, stashes, a merge or rebase stopped halfway.
GitHub: the phase PR; CI since the branch’s last green run.
docs/superpowers/: the spec’s status lines; the plan’s Now and boxes, Phase end’s included.
Commits since the newest close Task: a Plan: … Task N after it means Task N is open; a wip commit says where it stopped. Resume at the first task with no closing commit.
superpowers’ ledger, .superpowers/sdd/<plan file name without .md>/progress.md, before its runner starts: each task with a closing commit has a Task N: complete line, and no other task does. A line already there stays as it is; a new one reads Task N: complete (commits <base7>..<close7>, review clean), or , <K> parked instead of , review clean when the close parked findings. Nothing else changes. No ledger: create it, first line # SDD ledger — plan: <plan file>, then those lines only; mid-review, one fresh review runs from the task’s base.
Uncommitted work: run its tests; never touch it without Dan; untracked files by name only.
Q&A pages: what waits on Dan; on a vibed project, every “decided without Dan”.

The commits win where sources disagree, and the briefing says so: a task with no closing commit is open, whatever else says. The briefing, about 15 lines: phase, task, branch, the last commit’s age; done since Dan’s last OK; in flight, and its tests; decisions and rulings since the phase began, unseen ones marked; unpushed work and CI; what waits on Dan; changed diagrams, by link; then the next steps (Asking Dan). The go: a fresh session waits for Dan’s; “continue the plan” is one; after a compaction or usage-limit stop in a run he started, it stands. “Stop for today”: a wip commit, pushed under the standing OK, else ask.

title: 10  ubc-quarto-brand: how we work
text:
10.3 Each task’s loop
Seven steps, any model or harness, with subagents or inline. Record the task’s base first.

Build test-first: a commit after each green step (Commits), pushed under the standing OK.
Mechanical checks, before any reviewer: make check. It must cover the suite; the suite again under TZ=UTC and any other setting where CI differs; lint; the leak scan; and make docs on a site project. Read what it runs: anything it leaves out runs by its own target (make test-utc), never by hand.
Backward review after every build, whatever the build found or fixed: the tier’s review (Reviews), given the task, its scenario rows and the spec. Each finding: file and line, why, the fix, a severity, a decision (fix now, the phase-end list, or Dan). Grep the docs for each name the change renamed or removed, and for “not yet”, “planned”, “unverified” where it touched.
Forward review: read later tasks’ Consumes lines and later phases’ outlines; rewrite in the plan, now, every later listing that uses what changed, and name each under Forward:. Only the fifth stop (Stops) waits instead.
Docs: fix now what the change made untrue (a sentence, a status word, the README, a scenario row, a diagram: planned dashed, built solid). A missing page may wait, on the phase-end list.
Close: its own commit, before anything else starts, whatever the build’s step staged: the plan with this task’s boxes ticked, Now set to Task <N+1>: <title>, open., the forward rewrites, any “Built differently” and “Ruling:” lines, deferred findings on the phase-end list; the spec’s status line and scenario statuses; the close message (Commits). Only then the ledger’s Task N: complete line, naming it (executing-plans’ task-done runs now).
CI: closed once a run on its closing commit, or any later one on the branch, is green. A red run comes first: reopen the newest task closed before it (untick, reset Now) and fix it. No CI: the local checks are the gate, and the task closes on its closing commit.

A wrong listing is a planned test or code that fails a check, misses a scenario, or passes on one machine only. If building it right would change the spec, one of Dan’s decisions or a scenario’s expected outcome, it is the fifth stop (Stops). Otherwise it is drift: build it right, with a “Built differently” note at the task’s head (what, why, commits; the listing stays as planned) and the Drift: line. Fix-round dispatches carry the commit format and trailer. A bug a review missed is fixed with “escaped from Task N (Tier X), found by …” in the body.

10.4 Reviews








Tier
What
Review




1
if wrong, could take the system down, lose or leak data, or silently stop alerting
Matt’s code-review, two axes in two subagents, plus the security checklist; at most one re-review


2
feature code with tests, no safety role
Matt’s code-review, two axes in two subagents; fix Critical and Important; at most one re-review, only if a fix changed behaviour beyond its finding


3
docs, wording, display output, configs, test-only
a self-review under the two headings, plus the mechanical checks; Minor recorded, never looped; an Important fixed and counted




Matt Pocock’s code-review (mattpocock-skills:code-review) runs from the task’s base. Without it, his brief, short: two separate passes over git diff <base>...HEAD. Standards: breaks of the repo’s documented rules (cite them), and Fowler’s smells as judgement calls, the repo winning. Spec: missing or partial, not asked for, looks wrong; each quotes the spec line.
Security checklist: secrets, permissions, network exposure, failing closed, injection, logging; each item a line in the review, and under Rounds:: fine, a finding, or not applicable and why. At dispatch, say the tier and the review plan in one line.
Re-review: superpowers’ re-review-prompt.md; without it, “check each finding against the fix diff only, and whether the fix broke anything; not a fresh review”. No subagent tool: one pass per axis, each report in a file before the next; Rounds: says “self-review (no subagent tool)”.
Severity: Critical breaks a safety property, loses or leaks data, or blocks the phase (always to Dan); Important is a bug or missing case a user or test would hit, or a factually wrong doc; Minor is style, wording and nice-to-haves. The cap: re-reviews used up, a one-line fix is made directly, the rest goes to the phase-end list or Dan; never another round.

title: 10  ubc-quarto-brand: how we work
text:
10.5 Stops
The fifth stop: a change would alter the spec, one of Dan’s decisions or an approved scenario (its outcome, or moving it to Later or dropping it), or would remove the reason for a heavier later task (re-offer the simpler option). Attended, it is recorded and committed: a wip commit holding the question as item K on the phase’s Q&A page, and the plan’s Now reading, on one line, Task N stopped: waiting on Dan (Q&A, item K): <what conflicts with which scenario or decision>?; then that question (Asking Dan); nothing new starts. Vibed: a ruling, logged on the phase’s Q&A page as “decided without Dan”, in its commit body and in the next briefing. Attended runs on to an open, green phase PR, which waits for Dan’s merge; vibed merges it once CI is green and the phase end is done.
Never relaxed, in either mode: a leak-scan hit; force pushes, history rewrites (an amend or reset of a commit included), deleting branches or data; anything outside the repo (creating repos, publishing, sending messages); secrets, and spending money; weakening a guard (a check loosened or removed in the hooks, gitleaks.toml, leakcheck.py or CI’s leak or publish jobs; any allow marker or ignore entry added); the repo’s visibility; tags and releases; repo settings (rulesets, Pages, gh api writes, gh scopes); merging a PR you didn’t open, Dependabot’s too; an open Critical; a file the leak check couldn’t scan going out; a missing or invalid denylist. Also a stop: a diverged branch (ahead and behind, whatever the other side’s commits look like), or a merge or rebase stopped halfway: report it, never continue it. superpowers deleting its own git-ignored workspace is not “deleting data”.
A leak is a stop whether or not the repo has a remote, a hook or a leak check: what is committed gets pushed, and pushed history is permanent. A token, private address or personal name in the plan’s own listing is still a leak. On a hit, or text you’d expect to hit: commit nothing more, push nothing, no --no-verify, amend or reset; tell Dan its kind and file:line.

10.7 Pushing
The standing push OK, asked when a phase’s plan is approved, covers its branch (never main) until the phase merge: every commit is pushed. Without it, ask at each close. Text that leaves without git (PR text, merge messages, the repo description, comments) goes in a file, scanned by leakcheck.py --message and gitleaks stdin, then is sent with --body-file or read from the file into the flag.

10.9 Asking Dan

List first: every question or step in the batch, one line each, with the count.
One at a time: “Question N of M” and how many remain; say so when M changes.
A scenario: “Scenario: …. What do you expect?”, outcomes A., B., C., one recommended. Kickoff may open with one “describe it in your own words” question only when the request doesn’t say what the project is for or who uses it; naming what to build is not enough. In every other case the first question is a scenario too.
Self-review: a line just before it: what the recommendation was checked against (the evidence, Dan’s goals, the answers settled, what could go wrong), and what changed.
Selectable options where the harness has them (Claude Code’s AskUserQuestion, the recommended first, labelled “(Recommended)”); text when they need long explanation.
After each answer, the list again, answered items ticked ✓, then “Question N+1 of M”.
Record each answer on the Q&A page, with Dan’s reason in his words, and commit it then.
